title: Viability, Storage Stability, Release Kinetics, and Sensory Attributes of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 8014 in Synergistic Cryoprotectant‐Mediated Puree Blend
content:
Synergistic sodium alginate and glycerol protected Lactiplantibacillus plantarum in frozen pumpkin-carrot purée, maintaining probiotic viability above functional levels for 120 days. The formulation enabled controlled intestinal release, enhanced storage stability, and improved sensory acceptance, supporting its potential as a plant-based functional food.


ABSTRACT

Two synergistic cryoprotectants, glycerol and sodium alginate (SA), were evaluated for their impact on survival, simulated gastrointestinal tolerance and sensory quality of the probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum in a frozen fruit puree. L. plantarum was added to purees along with different cryoprotectant mixture combinations and stored at sub-zero temperatures for 4 months. Microbiological, physicochemical and sensory properties were determined during storage. The probiotic viability (6.59–7.33 log10 CFU/mL) of the samples treated with cryoprotectant was higher than that of the controls, indicating good cryoprotection and stability. High resistance and a controlled release in the simulated intestine were achieved through simulated digestion, yielding viable counts between 5.20 and 5.64 log10 CFU/mL after 5 h. In the sensory evaluation, formulations that included cryoprotectants were noted for their overall acceptability, consistency, and taste. The results indicate that both glycerol and sodium alginate are promising candidates for developing functional foods, as they help maintain probiotic stability during frozen storage, facilitate effective gastrointestinal delivery, and enhance consumer acceptance.
